explanation: Seen straight on, it is a pale smear; from the side, it becomes a skull, a reminder of death. The perspective trick is called anamorphosis.

claims.text: Hans Holbein's The Ambassadors (1533) shows a distorted skull stretched across the floor.
The distorted shape on the floor of The Ambassadors is not a sword, a serpent or a candle.
The skull in The Ambassadors becomes recognizable only when viewed from a sharp angle to the side.
The skull is commonly read as a memento mori, a reminder of death.
The distortion technique is called anamorphosis.
